permeate

/PUR-mee-ayt/ - the stress falls on PUR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Permeate means to spread throughout, saturate.

Let the campfire burn ten minutes and its smoke will permeate every sweater in the tent.

Example

Within a season, the new coach's calm had permeated the whole club — players stopped arguing calls, the bench chatter turned tactical, and even the parents in the stands quieted down.

Permeate is more thorough than 'spread' — what spreads can stay patchy, but what permeates works into every part of a thing, the way dye permeates cloth or a rumor permeates a small town.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

pervade: Pervade describes the finished state: a mood or smell that is simply present everywhere, an atmosphere already in place. Permeate is the verb of the process — the working-in, the soaking-through, dye taking cloth fiber by fiber. Once something has fully permeated a place, we say the place is pervaded by it.

suffuse: Suffuse is gentle and usually lovely — light suffusing a room, a blush suffusing a face, color spreading softly through something. Permeate is more thorough and more physical: it works into every fiber and pocket of a thing, smoke into sweaters, damp into plaster. Suffuse tints; permeate saturates.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

evaporate: to thin away and vanish rather than sink in

recede: to withdraw and leave the thing untouched

Where it sits · how thoroughly it soaks through

seep → permeate → drench

seep vs. permeate: Seep stops short of permeate — seeping is the slow leak at one edge, while permeating reaches every fiber of the thing.

drench vs. permeate: Drench goes further than permeate — what permeates fills a thing through; what drenches leaves it streaming, past holding any more.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — per-: through

Root — mea-: to pass, to go (Latin meare)

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do (verb-forming)

Put it together: Per- ('through') + mea- (Latin meare, 'to pass') + -ate = to pass through. What permeates literally goes through and through — smoke through wool, water through limestone, a mood through a locker room — until no part is left out.

Use the root in a new word: impermeable: A good rain shell is impermeable — water beads and rolls off instead of passing through.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / precise

Permeate is the careful word for total penetration — smells, moisture, moods, ideas. Spread says motion outward; soak says wetness; permeate says every part has been reached. Its cousin pervade describes the finished state; permeate, the working-in.
